correctness.rationale: For k>=3 parallel positive-length arcs, direct-vs-other-path series-parallel reduction gives R(A,X_i(x))=x-(l_i-rho)x^2/l_i², rho=(sum l_i^-1)^-1. On long arcs l_i>2rho the unique interior maximum is l_i²/[4(l_i-rho)]; the longest m>=k rho is in this regime, and f(l) increases for l>2rho. Thus E=m²/[4(m-rho)]. The larger quadratic root m=2E+2sqrt(E(E-rho)) recovers maximal arc; k=3 the residual two lengths follow sum L-m and reciprocal C=rho^-1-m^-1. At k>=4 [5,1,2,3] versus [5,1.5,2.25±.75 sqrt(15/7)] share (L=11,rho=30/61,E) but are nonisometric; vary a shorter length locally to obtain continuum. Fixed-L bound L/[4(k-1)]<=E<L/4 by reciprocal convexity/majorization, equal-arc equality. Independently checked exact Kirchhoff reductions and scalar inversions and 4-arm example; simulations are not infinite proofs.
